literal: Hostility he does not see, prosperity when coming; that, magnifying he will see, ruin to bring.
translation: When prosperity is on its way, a person does not look for hostility; but when ruin is about to be brought upon him, he will seek to magnify that very hostility.
modern: செல்வம் வரும்போது ஒருவன் பகைமையை நாடமாட்டான்; ஆனால் அவனுக்குக் கேடு வரும்போது, அவன் அந்தப் பகைமையை வளர்க்கவே விரும்புவான்.
explanation: This couplet explains how a person's attitude toward hostility (ikal) indicates their impending fortune or ruin. When prosperity (akkam) is about to arrive, a person naturally avoids or ignores discord. Conversely, when ruin (ketu) is destined to come, the person actively seeks out and magnifies (mikal) that hostility. Thus, one's inclination to foster or avoid conflict serves as a clear sign of their future state.
